question: Explain what happens when a dielectric is placed in an external electric field. Why does the net electric field inside the dielectric become smaller than the applied field?

options.A: The dielectric develops free charges that strengthen the applied field inside it
options.B: The external field polarises the dielectric; bound charges produce an induced field opposite to the applied field, so the net field is reduced
options.C: The electric field inside a dielectric becomes zero because it behaves as a conductor
options.D: The molecules rotate randomly and produce an induced field in the same direction as the applied field
